title: Salsa Verde Mexicana
subtitle: Mexican green tomatillo and chilli sauce
excerpt: Mexican salsa verde is a blended green sauce made from tomatillos, green chillies, garlic, coriander, and onion. It is cooked briefly to develop the flavour, unlike pico de gallo which is raw. The characteristic tart, slightly fruity flavour of tomatillo makes this a completely different sauce from Italian salsa verde.
sourceNotes: Mexican salsa verde (green sauce) has Aztec origins: tomatillos (tomate verde) were central to Aztec cooking and were already used in sauces long before the Spanish arrived. The cooked version (toasting or roasting the tomatillos before blending) is the traditional Mexican method and produces a more complex, slightly smoky flavour than raw blended salsa verde.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales directly. Make a large batch and freeze in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days.

content.text: Tinned tomatillos are reliable in the UK and produce a good result. If using fresh, remove the husks and rinse off the sticky coating before cooking. The brief frying step after blending concentrates the sauce and develops the colour from bright green to a more muted olive: both are correct, but the fried (cooked) version has more depth.

items.prepNote: or jalapeños, seeds removed for less heat

content.text: If using fresh tomatillos: put them in a dry frying pan with the chillies and garlic over medium-high heat. Toast, turning, for 5 minutes until charred in places and softened. If using tinned tomatillos: skip this step and drain them before blending.
Blend the tomatillos, chillies, garlic, onion, and coriander until smooth. Season with salt and lime juice.

Heat the sunflower oil in the same frying pan over high heat. Pour in the blended salsa. It will spit and bubble immediately. Fry, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce darkens slightly and deepens in flavour. Taste and adjust with more salt or lime.

Use as a dip with tortilla chips, as a sauce for enchiladas verdes, spooned over tacos, or used as a cooking liquid for chicken (pollo en salsa verde). It is also excellent on eggs or as a dressing for roasted vegetables.
